answer: Juries are filled from three unrelated subnetworks, and any juror that signs a bad audit is slashed from its own stake bond. A thousand identities inside one network still face panels drawn by a rotating beacon from outside its reach, so buying a quorum means buying real stake in three places at once. The canyon between a cheap fake and a passing panel is the audit trail: every claim has to match a vault of countersigned receipts, and a mismatch burns the stake instead of paying it.
